hero.headline: Apple announces partnerships with Google and Nvidia for AI model powering Siri updates
hero.body:
Apple unveiled a significant overhaul to its Siri voice assistant at its annual Worldwide Developers Conference, marking a major shift for the company's approach to artificial intelligence. The new Siri, branded as "Siri AI," will be integrated with Apple Intelligence and rolled out to users in the fall.

Tim Cook highlighted the Siri improvements during his final WWDC keynote, positioning the upgrade as a response to years of user frustration with the assistant's limitations. The revamped Siri will function more like advanced AI chatbots such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini rather than a traditional search tool that pulls information from the web.

The announcement represents a departure from Apple's historical practice of developing core technologies internally. The company focused on practical improvements to Siri rather than presenting flashy new features, though the underlying AI technology represents a substantial advancement.

Apple introduced its third generation of foundation models, which will power the new Siri capabilities and other features in iOS 27. These models are designed to handle a broader range of tasks and understand more complex user requests than previous versions. The foundation models were developed using infrastructure and expertise that goes beyond Apple's own research teams, signaling the company's recognition that advanced AI development increasingly requires external collaboration.

The new Siri will be available as part of iOS 27, Apple's next mobile operating system. Developers will gain access to testing versions of the software before a public release later this year. The company published technical details about the foundation models alongside the keynote announcement.

In addition to the Siri upgrades, Apple revealed a series of new child safety features amid ongoing scrutiny over apps that create sexual images of children. These safety features address concerns raised by UK Prime Minister Starmer, who called on Apple and Google to activate built-in protections that prevent children from accessing sexually explicit material on their devices.

The company also emphasized its traditional approach of prioritizing privacy and on-device processing, even as it pursues partnerships to accelerate AI development. This combination of external collaboration and privacy-focused design reflects Apple's attempt to balance rapid AI advancement with user protection.

The Siri AI announcement comes as technology companies compete to integrate increasingly powerful artificial intelligence into consumer products. Apple has faced questions in recent years about whether it is keeping pace with competitors in AI capabilities. The Siri improvements and related iOS 27 announcements suggest Apple is working to address these concerns while maintaining its distinctive approach to technology development.

cards.headline: U.S.-Iran Peace Talks Face Obstacles as Both Sides Seek Victory
cards.teaser: Washington and Tehran each need to present any agreement as a win, complicating negotiations already strained by leadership approaches.
cards.body:
Washington and Tehran face a fundamental challenge in negotiations: each government must present any agreement as a victory to its domestic audience. This requirement complicates talks that mediators already describe as difficult, given the leadership styles involved on both sides.

The pressure to frame deals as advantageous creates additional friction in negotiations that involve multiple disputed issues. Both nations struggle to balance the political necessity of claiming success with the compromises required for a breakthrough agreement.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Lebanese City of Tyre as New Cease-Fire Falters
cards.body:
Israel bombed the southern Lebanese city of Tyre following evacuation warnings for the entire city, raising questions about the durability of a brief cease-fire between Israel and Iran. The strikes came one day after Iran warned it would attack Israel if the country continued its military offensive in southern Lebanon.

The bombardment of Tyre represents a significant escalation in Israel's campaign against Hezbollah, the Lebanese militia backed by Iran. Israel issued evacuation orders for the entire coastal city before launching the strikes, though the extent of casualties and damage remains unclear. The city has been a stronghold of Hezbollah influence in southern Lebanon.

The attack follows a day in which Israel and Iran appeared to pull back from direct confrontation. Iran had previously threatened retaliation if Israel maintained its offensive against Hezbollah positions in Lebanon. The Israeli military operation against the Lebanese militia has emerged as a major obstacle in ongoing peace negotiations between the United States and Iran.

The situation in southern Lebanon has become a focal point in broader regional tensions. The U.S.-Iran peace talks have sought to address multiple points of conflict, but Israel's continued operations against Hezbollah have complicated diplomatic efforts. Iran has maintained its support for Hezbollah as part of its regional strategy, while Israel views the group as a direct security threat on its northern border.

The fragility of the cease-fire arrangement became apparent within 24 hours of the pullback from direct confrontation. The cycle of warnings, evacuations, and strikes suggests that a lasting resolution to the conflict remains distant, even as international mediators work to prevent a wider regional war.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall After Israel and Iran Halt Strikes
cards.teaser: Crude prices declined following an agreement between the two nations to cease military attacks.
cards.body:
Oil prices eased after Israel and Iran agreed to halt strikes against each other, reducing concerns about escalating regional conflict. The temporary cessation of hostilities relieved pressure on energy markets that had spiked due to fears of disrupted supplies from the Persian Gulf.

The agreement follows a period of heightened Middle East tensions that threatened shipping lanes critical to crude oil transportation. Energy markets had factored in risk premiums reflecting the possibility that expanded military action could affect regional oil production and global supply chains.

cards.headline: U.S. military helicopter crashes near Strait of Hormuz, crew rescued
cards.body:
A U.S. Army Apache attack helicopter crashed near the Strait of Hormuz, with both crew members successfully rescued following the incident. President Trump confirmed that the pilots were "fine" after the crash, which occurred amid escalating tensions in the region.

The rescue operation was completed without casualties, according to military officials. The incident took place in a strategically critical area where the United States maintains an active military presence to protect shipping lanes and monitor regional activity.

The Strait of Hormuz represents one of the world's most important maritime chokepoints, with roughly one-fifth of global petroleum passing through the narrow waterway that connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman. U.S. military forces regularly patrol the area as part of broader security operations designed to safeguard commercial shipping and project American power in the Middle East.

The helicopter crash occurred during a period of heightened military activity and diplomatic tensions. The situation has been further complicated by recent U.S. military operations in the region, including the seizure of an Iranian-flagged container ship that attempted to bypass an American blockade near the strait. U.S. Central Command reported that Marines departed the USS Tripoli assault ship by helicopter and rappelled onto the vessel, which the U.S. Navy had disabled by firing on its engine room after it refused to stop.

Iran's military command responded to the ship seizure by warning that Tehran would "soon respond and retaliate against this armed piracy and the US military." The incident strained ongoing peace negotiations, with Iranian state media reporting that Tehran had rejected new talks, citing the ongoing blockade, threatening rhetoric, and what officials described as Washington's shifting positions and excessive demands.

Trump had previously indicated optimism about reaching a peace agreement with Iran, suggesting that negotiations could yield results within days. He stated that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen immediately following any deal, implying that current restrictions or tensions were affecting passage through the waterway.

The escalating military confrontation threatens to worsen an already severe global energy crisis and risks pushing the two countries toward renewed conflict. The ongoing tensions have resulted in significant casualties on multiple sides, with at least 3,000 people killed in Iran, nearly 2,300 in Lebanon, 23 civilians and 15 soldiers in Israel, and more than a dozen in Gulf Arab states. Thirteen U.S. service members have also been killed during the conflict.

The cause of the Apache helicopter crash has not been disclosed by military officials. The incident underscores the operational risks facing American forces deployed in the region during this period of active military operations and diplomatic uncertainty.

cards.headline: House takes up reconciliation bill as Republicans weigh immigration enforcement votes
cards.teaser: The House of Representatives began consideration of a reconciliation bill on Tuesday, as Republican leaders work to secure support for a separate immigration en.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives began consideration of a reconciliation bill on Tuesday. Republican leaders are working to secure support for a separate immigration enforcement measure, though party leaders remain uncertain whether they have enough votes to pass it.

President Trump said late Monday that two crew members aboard a U.S. attack helicopter that crashed near the Strait of Hormuz are "fine." The AH-64 Apache helicopter was patrolling regional waters when it went down near the Oman coast, according to U.S. Central Command.

cards.headline: Trump appointee Bill Pulte named director of national intelligence
cards.teaser: President Trump appointed Bill Pulte as interim director of national intelligence despite his lack of intelligence or national security experience.
cards.body:
President Trump named Bill Pulte as interim director of national intelligence, despite Pulte having no background in intelligence or national security. The appointment places Pulte in charge of overseeing the nation's intelligence agencies and coordinating their activities.

The stated reason for Pulte's appointment is to investigate claims that the 2020 presidential election was stolen. Pulte will serve in an interim capacity heading the intelligence community while pursuing this goal.

cards.headline: Drones From Ukraine War Veer Off Course Into Neighboring Countries
cards.teaser: Drones launched by both Russia and Ukraine are straying from their intended targets and entering countries not involved in the conflict.
cards.body:
Drones deployed by Russian and Ukrainian forces are veering off course and flying over neighboring nations, creating new security concerns for countries not directly involved in the war. The errant aircraft have prompted residents in border regions to seek shelter as the unmanned vehicles pass overhead.

The incidents highlight an unintended consequence of the widespread use of drone warfare in the Ukraine conflict. Countries sharing borders with Ukraine face the challenge of responding to military hardware entering their airspace without being parties to the conflict themselves.

cards.headline: Kenyan Police Use Tear Gas on Protesters Opposing U.S. Ebola Quarantine Center
cards.teaser: Demonstrations erupted over plans for a U.S.-linked Ebola treatment facility near the border, with protesters citing infection risks and lack of government transparency.
cards.body:
Kenyan police deployed tear gas against demonstrators protesting plans to establish an Ebola quarantine and treatment center with U.S. involvement. The protesters raised concerns about the risk of infectious disease spreading across borders from the proposed facility.

Community members also criticized the Kenyan government for failing to involve them in decision-making about the medical center. Demonstrators questioned why they had not been consulted about hosting a facility designed to treat one of the world's most dangerous infectious diseases.

cards.headline: Iran's World Cup Ticket Allocation Revoked Days Before Tournament
cards.teaser: Iran's football federation says its tickets for the group stage were revoked just days before the World Cup begins.
cards.body:
Iran's football federation announced that its ticket allocation for the World Cup group stage has been revoked just days before the tournament begins. The federation had already started selling tickets to fans but can no longer provide them.

Iran is scheduled to play three group matches in the United States: against New Zealand and Belgium in Los Angeles on June 15 and 21 respectively, and against Egypt in Seattle on June 26. The sudden revocation leaves Iranian supporters who made travel arrangements unable to attend their team's matches. The federation said the decision "raises questions about interference of non-sporting considerations."

cards.headline: War Leaves Lebanese City of Nabatieh Reflecting Nation's Fears
cards.teaser: The city of Nabatieh, once a symbol of Lebanon's changing fortunes, now represents the country's deepest concerns amid ongoing conflict.
cards.body:
Nabatieh, a city that once served as a barometer for Lebanon's economic and social shifts, has become a symbol of the country's gravest fears as war continues without end. The southern Lebanese city has experienced transformation as military conflict reshapes daily life.

The city's trajectory mirrors broader Lebanese anxieties about the future. What residents once called the roar of commerce and community life has been replaced by the sounds of a cease-fire that offers no guarantee of lasting peace.

cards.headline: Somali World Cup Referee Denied Entry to United States
cards.teaser: Omar Artan was removed from the list of officials after being barred from entering the U.S., where the tournament will be held.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, who would have been the first Somali referee to officiate at a World Cup finals, has been dropped from the tournament's officiating roster after U.S. authorities denied him entry to the country.

The decision means Somalia will have no representation among the officials working at the World Cup being hosted in the United States.

cards.headline: Man convicted in first sex-based harassment prosecution sentenced
cards.teaser: David Stroud received a sentence after being found guilty in a landmark case prosecuting hair-grabbing and unwanted advances as sex-based harassment.
cards.body:
David Stroud was sentenced following his conviction in May for grabbing a woman's hair and asking for a kiss. The case marked the first prosecution of its kind for sex-based harassment.

The conviction established a legal precedent for prosecuting physical harassment that does not rise to the level of assault but involves unwanted sexual advances.

cards.headline: Four states hold primary elections
cards.teaser: Voters in four states cast ballots in primary elections to select candidates for upcoming general elections.
cards.body:
Primary elections took place in four states, with voters selecting party nominees for various offices. The contests determine which candidates will advance to general election ballots later this year.

The primaries unfold as part of the regular election cycle, with races at multiple levels of government on the ballot. Results will shape the November electoral landscape in the participating states.

cards.headline: Trump claims California vote fraud without evidence
cards.teaser: The president made unfounded allegations of electoral fraud in California, previewing arguments likely to feature in fall campaign strategy.
cards.body:
Trump is "inventing fraud" in California's primary elections, according to pro-democracy experts. The president has employed this strategy repeatedly throughout his career, from disputing Emmy losses to contesting his 2020 election defeat. Critics warn he is likely to escalate unfounded fraud allegations when additional races don't go his way.

Election integrity campaigners express concern that this time could prove different, with Trump loyalists positioned in key roles to amplify his message. The allegations emerged as California vote counting continued, with the state experiencing a "red mirage"—where early returns differ from final tallies as various ballot types are counted at different times.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass faces November runoff against progressive challenger
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman advanced to a runoff election against incumbent Mayor Karen Bass after finishing second in the primary.
cards.body:
Progressive candidate Nithya Raman advanced to a November runoff against incumbent Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass after securing second place in the mayoral race. Raman defeated Spencer Pratt, a reality television personality from The Hills, who failed to advance to the general election.

Raman, described as a left-wing candidate, expressed being "incredibly honoured" by her advancement. She vowed to "fight for a healthier, safer and more joyful Los Angeles" in the upcoming contest that will determine leadership of the nation's second-largest city.

cards.headline: Iran's World Cup ticket allocation revoked days before tournament
cards.teaser: FIFA revoked Iran's allocation of group stage tickets just days before the World Cup begins, according to the country's football federation.
cards.body:
Iran's football federation said its World Cup ticket allocation was revoked just days before the tournament began, preventing fans from attending group stage matches. The federation had already started selling tickets to supporters who made travel arrangements to watch Iran play New Zealand on June 15 and Belgium on June 21 in Los Angeles, followed by Egypt on June 26 in Seattle.

The Iranian federation stated the decision "raises questions about interference of non-sporting considerations," suggesting it viewed the revocation as politically motivated rather than sports-related.

cards.headline: Man sentenced for murder of partner after setting home ablaze
cards.teaser: Clifton George received a prison sentence for stabbing Annabel Rook 31 times and starting a fire at their north London home.
cards.body:
Clifton George has been jailed for the murder of his partner Annabel Rook at their home in north London. George stabbed Rook 31 times before setting fire to the property in Stoke Newington.

The attack followed Rook's attempt to end their relationship.

hero.headline: GSK to Acquire Cancer Drugmaker Nuvalent for $10.6 Billion
hero.body:
British pharmaceutical company GSK has agreed to buy Nuvalent, a Boston-based cancer biotech firm, for $10.6 billion in what marks the company's largest acquisition ever. GSK will pay $124 per share in cash, sending Nuvalent shares surging 39 percent in premarket trading.

The deal represents a significant expansion of GSK's oncology portfolio and reflects new chief executive Luke Miels' aggressive push into cancer treatments. Miels, who took over at the start of the year, described the acquisition as part of a "brick-by-brick approach" to strengthen the company's drug pipeline.

Nuvalent specializes in developing precision oncology treatments, particularly for lung cancer. The acquisition gives GSK access to two late-stage drugs with major commercial potential. Zidesamtinib and neladalkib are being reviewed by the US Food and Drug Administration, with decisions expected in September and November. Both drugs target non-small cell lung cancer and are expected to launch later this year if approved. Analysts project these could become multi-blockbuster drugs, each generating several billion dollars annually.

The treatments target specific genetic mutations that drive lung cancer in non-smoking adults aged 40 to 50, predominantly women, affecting approximately 4,000 people in the US. Both drugs aim to provide longer effective treatment with improved tolerability and quality of life compared to current options. Miels noted that existing lung cancer treatments require seven to eight years of therapy and often cause patients to gain significant weight. "These are relatively young people. They've got kids, they lead active lives," he said. "Clearly there's a gap for a much better-tolerated product."

Nuvalent was founded in 2017 by Matthew Shair, a Harvard chemistry professor, and went public on the Nasdaq in 2021. Shair holds a 2.16 percent stake and is in line to receive just under $200 million from the sale. Deerfield Management, a New York-based healthcare investment firm, is the company's largest shareholder.

The deal was more than a year in the making, according to Miels, who praised Nuvalent's scientists as an "impressive group of people." GSK also expects to gain a platform for rapid expansion in lung cancer through a pipeline drug called Ris-Rez, which is in late-stage development and targets multiple cancer forms.

This acquisition follows GSK's earlier deal in January to buy California biotech company RAPT for $2.2 billion, which is developing a treatment for severe food allergies. The Nuvalent purchase positions GSK to improve profit contributions from 2027 and supports the company's target of more than 40 billion pounds in annual sales by 2031.

cards.headline: OpenAI Files for Stock Market Debut
cards.teaser: The company behind ChatGPT filed plans for an initial public offering, setting up competition with rival Anthropic.
cards.body:
OpenAI has filed confidentially to go public on the US stock market, according to an announcement from the company. The AI giant is expected to be valued at more than $850 billion, making it one of the most highly valued listings in market history. OpenAI noted that it hasn't decided on timing for the debut and may remain private for a while longer to pursue initiatives easier to execute as a private company.

The filing comes as multiple major technology companies prepare for public market debuts. Anthropic has also submitted IPO plans, and SpaceX is considering a stock offering. Analysts have raised questions about whether the market can absorb these simultaneous giant offerings from the AI and technology sectors.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Preparation Draws Investor Interest
cards.teaser: The space exploration company's planned initial public offering has prompted questions about valuation and passive investing strategies.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for its stock market debut on June 12 with a valuation of $135 per share. The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares, raising approximately $75 billion in what is being billed as the largest initial public offering in history.

Up to a quarter of the shares will be reserved for individual investors rather than institutional funds and banks—a notably larger allocation to retail investors than is typical for IPOs of this scale. Experts have flagged potential risks associated with the offering.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall After Israel and Iran Halt Strikes
cards.teaser: Crude prices declined following an agreement between the two nations to cease military attacks.
cards.body:
Oil prices eased after Israel and Iran agreed to halt strikes against each other, reducing concerns about escalating regional conflict. The temporary cessation of hostilities relieved pressure on energy markets that had spiked due to fears of disrupted supplies from the Persian Gulf.

The agreement follows a period of heightened Middle East tensions that threatened shipping lanes critical to crude oil transportation. Energy markets had factored in risk premiums reflecting the possibility that expanded military action could affect regional oil production and global supply chains.

cards.headline: Dubai Economy Faces Pressure From Regional Conflict
cards.teaser: The city's reliance on trade and travel has become a vulnerability as war with Iran affects the Persian Gulf.
cards.body:
Dubai's economy is being tested by the ongoing conflict with Iran, as the city's dependence on international trade and travel creates exposure to regional instability. The war has disrupted normal commerce patterns in the Persian Gulf, affecting Dubai's position as a trade and logistics hub.

The emirate built its economic model around serving as a connection point for global business, with major industries including aviation, shipping, tourism, and financial services. Regional conflict threatens these sectors by reducing travel demand and complicating trade routes. Dubai's economic resilience is being measured by its ability to maintain business activity despite geopolitical tensions affecting the broader Gulf region.

cards.headline: US Exports Rose 2.6 Percent in April
cards.teaser: Commerce Department data showed exports increased to $327.1 billion as war with Iran boosted oil demand.
cards.body:
US exports rose 2.6 percent in April to $327.1 billion, according to Commerce Department data. The increase was partly driven by oil demand related to the war with Iran, which disrupted regional energy supplies and boosted demand for American crude.

Energy products played a significant role in the export growth as global buyers sought alternative oil sources amid uncertainty over Middle Eastern availability.

cards.headline: Stock Futures Point to Market Recovery
cards.teaser: Nasdaq futures indicated further gains as chip stocks continued rebounding and major IPOs remained in focus.
cards.body:
US stock futures climbed in premarket trading, with Nasdaq futures signaling continued gains as semiconductor stocks extended their rebound. Dow futures rose 125 points ahead of the opening bell. Technology stocks led the advance, particularly chip manufacturers and AI-related hardware companies.

SpaceX and OpenAI's planned stock market debuts remain focal points for investors. Oil prices declined as geopolitical tensions eased, providing additional support for equity markets.

cards.headline: NASA to announce Artemis 3 moon mission crew and provide mission updates
cards.teaser: NASA will unveil the astronauts selected for the Artemis 3 lunar landing mission and share updates on the program's progress.
cards.body:
NASA will unveil the astronauts selected for the Artemis 3 mission and share updates on the program's progress. The announcement will be available through live coverage.

Artemis 3 represents a major milestone in lunar exploration, aiming to land humans on the moon's surface for the first time in decades. The mission builds on NASA's broader plans for sustained lunar presence, which include deploying hopping drones and roving vehicles to support a permanent moon base.

cards.headline: Researchers confirm wind flowing from the Milky Way's central black hole
cards.teaser: Scientists have detected active wind from the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, confirming decades of theoretical predictions.
cards.body:
Observations have revealed that the supermassive black hole at the heart of the Milky Way produces wind, a phenomenon theorists have predicted for more than half a century. The discovery confirms that even relatively quiet black holes generate outflows of material. The findings resolve a longstanding question about the galactic center.

The wind was detected through new observations of the Milky Way's central region. Scientists had theorized that the black hole must be exhaling material based on models of black hole behavior, but direct evidence remained elusive until now. The discovery provides insights into how black holes interact with their surrounding environments.

cards.headline: iOS 27 code reveals references to foldable iPhone in development
cards.teaser: Apple's iOS 27 beta software contains multiple hints about a foldable iPhone, including new frameworks and app resizability features.
cards.body:
Code within iOS 27 includes references that suggest Apple is developing a foldable iPhone. The beta version contains new framework strings and features focused on app resizability, which would be necessary for a device with a folding screen. Bloomberg and other outlets identified the references within the software.

The hints include infrastructure for apps to adapt to different screen configurations dynamically. Apple has not officially announced a foldable iPhone, but the code suggests the company is preparing its operating system for such a device. The references mirror preparations other manufacturers made before launching foldable phones.

cards.headline: Instagram releases feature allowing users to reorder posts on profile grid
cards.teaser: Meta introduced a tool that lets Instagram users rearrange posts on their profile grids, addressing one of the platform's most requested features.
cards.body:
Instagram users can now rearrange posts on their profile grids with a feature that's rolling out via mobile apps on Android and iPhone. The ability to reorder published photos and videos was announced nearly a year ago and had been tested with select users before the wider release on June 8th.

Previously, Instagram posts appeared in reverse chronological order with no way to rearrange them without deleting and reposting. The new tool gives users greater control over how their profiles appear to visitors.

cards.headline: Jupiter and Venus appear in close conjunction visible tonight
cards.teaser: Jupiter and Venus will appear very close together in the night sky, creating a conjunction visible without a telescope.
cards.body:
Jupiter and Venus will align in the night sky this week in a rare conjunction that makes them appear extremely close together. The two planets will be visible to the naked eye without any telescope needed.

This celestial event occurs when the orbital paths of Jupiter and Venus align from Earth's perspective, positioning them side by side in the night sky. Observers in most locations with clear skies can view the phenomenon over the coming nights.

cards.headline: Zepto files for IPO showing revenue growth and increased losses
cards.teaser: Indian quick commerce company Zepto revealed fast revenue growth and larger operating losses in its public offering filing.
cards.body:
Zepto disclosed financial results in its initial public offering filing, showing operating revenue growth of 104 percent year-over-year. The company's advertising business grew even faster, with advertising revenue jumping 151 percent and outpacing overall revenue expansion.

Operating losses also increased during the same period. The quick commerce company, which delivers groceries and goods in minutes, now faces questions about its valuation ahead of its stock market debut as it competes in an increasingly crowded market.

hero.headline: Teen Miles Russell qualifies for U.S. Open with Charlie Woods as caddie
hero.teaser: Russell endured Golf's Longest Day to earn a spot in next week's U.S. Open.
hero.body:
Miles Russell, a teenager, qualified for next week's U.S. Open with Tiger Woods' son Charlie Woods serving as his caddie. Russell was among the golfers who competed through the lengthy qualifying process known as Golf's Longest Day.

The pairing drew attention for the presence of Woods' son on the bag as Russell navigated the pressure of qualifying. Russell will now compete in one of golf's four major championships when the U.S. Open begins next week.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark hits game-winning three-pointer with 1.2 seconds left for Fever
cards.teaser: Clark's late shot gave Indiana a 78-76 victory over Washington on Monday night.
cards.body:
Caitlin Clark delivered a clutch three-pointer with 1.2 seconds remaining to lift the Indiana Fever to a 78-76 victory over the Washington Mystics on Monday night. The shot came after the Fever had trailed late in the game.

Clark's performance continues to showcase her ability to perform under pressure during her rookie WNBA season. She reflected on the moment, noting that she was able to block out the surrounding noise to focus on the shot.

cards.headline: Spurs cut Knicks series lead to 2-1 with Game 3 win at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The San Antonio Spurs defeated the New York Knicks in Game 3 of the NBA Finals on Monday night at Madison Square Garden, narrowing the series deficit to 2-1.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama delivered 32 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the San Antonio Spurs defeated the New York Knicks 115-111 on Monday night, trimming the series deficit to 2-1. The victory represented a return to form for San Antonio after losing the first two games at home.

The spectacle at Madison Square Garden extended beyond the court, with President Donald Trump attending the game alongside other high-profile attendees. The Knicks maintain their series advantage heading into Game 4, where the Spurs will attempt to even the Finals.

cards.headline: FIFA revokes Iran fan ticket allocation for World Cup games in United States
cards.teaser: Iran's national football federation said FIFA pulled tickets for fans at all three group stage matches.
cards.body:
FIFA has revoked the ticket allocation for Iran fans attending the team's three World Cup group stage matches in the United States, according to Iran's national football federation. The decision was announced Tuesday and applies to all of Iran's matches during the tournament.

The 2026 World Cup will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico, with Iran scheduled to play its group stage games on American soil.

cards.headline: Judge rules Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby eligible, drawing widespread criticism
cards.teaser: College coaches and athletic directors reacted strongly to Monday's ruling, with some Big 12 schools discussing not playing the Red Raiders.
cards.body:
A judge ruled Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby eligible on Monday, prompting sharp reactions from college football coaches and athletic directors across the country. Multiple coaches described the decision as a sad day for the sport, with responses ranging from dire predictions about the future to practical concerns about competitive fairness.

Some Big 12 schools have informally discussed the possibility of refusing to play Texas Tech as a result of the ruling. Athletic directors expressed being stunned by the decision, which could have broader implications for eligibility disputes in college athletics.

cards.headline: Brandon Aiyuk posts video appearing to suggest 49ers afraid to release him
cards.teaser: The wide receiver shared an Instagram video Sunday implying San Francisco fears he could make them regret letting him go.
cards.body:
Brandon Aiyuk posted a video on Instagram Sunday that appeared to imply the San Francisco 49ers fear releasing him. The message suggested the team is worried he could sign with another franchise and eventually become a problem for them down the line.

The post marks another development in the ongoing situation between Aiyuk and the 49ers. Contract negotiations between the wide receiver and the team have remained a point of ongoing discussion.

cards.headline: NFL teams complete multiple trades on key June day
cards.teaser: More than 15 coaches, players and executives provided insight into the back-to-back deals.
cards.body:
The NFL saw a flurry of trading activity on a significant June day, with multiple deals completed in quick succession. More than 15 coaches, players and team executives shed light on the transactions that reshaped several rosters.

The trades ranged from moves addressing salary cap issues to teams positioning themselves for the upcoming season. League insiders described the day as notable for both the volume and timing of the deals.

hero.headline: Ariana Grande and Ethan Slater Split After Three Years
hero.body:
Pop star Ariana Grande and actor Ethan Slater have ended their relationship after nearly three years together, according to multiple reports. The couple met while working together on the first Wicked film, where Grande played Glinda and Slater portrayed Boq.

Grande's performance in the musical adaptation earned her significant recognition, including an Oscar nomination. The film became a major commercial success, collecting $765 million at the worldwide box office and winning two Academy Awards.

Grande and Slater made their relationship public in 2023, following the end of their previous relationships. Their romance generated considerable media attention at the time due to the circumstances surrounding their coupling and their high-profile status in entertainment.

Slater is known for his theatrical work, including a Tony-nominated performance in SpongeBob SquarePants: The Musical. He joined the Wicked cast in a supporting role alongside Grande, who is an acclaimed Grammy-winning musician with a large global following.

Neither Grande nor Slater has issued a public statement regarding the split. The breakup comes as both continue advancing their careers in their respective fields. Grande maintains an active presence in music while Slater pursues acting work.

Sources close to the situation have not revealed specific details about what led to the separation or how it might affect their professional obligations to the Wicked franchise, given that both starred in the first film and appear set to continue with upcoming sequels.

The couple had maintained a relatively private relationship throughout their time together, despite their celebrity status. After the initial media coverage when they first became public, they generally avoided extensive public displays of their romance.

The Wicked film series has been significant in Grande's career, marking a major transition from her work as a recording artist to the film industry. The first installment's critical and commercial success established her as a serious actress, though subsequent projects in the franchise have performed differently at the box office.

Slater's involvement in the Wicked adaptations represents a continuation of his work across both stage and screen productions. His casting in the musical film series built upon his established reputation in theatrical performances.

As both entertainers navigate life following the separation, they will likely continue to engage with professional commitments that may require them to interact, particularly regarding the Wicked franchise that brought them together initially.

cards.headline: Nick Reiner Seeks Access to Trust Fund Left by Parents for Murder Defense
cards.teaser: The son of director Rob Reiner is requesting money from a trust his parents established to fund his legal defense against charges in their killings.
cards.body:
Nick Reiner, son of filmmaker Rob Reiner, has filed a request to access a $1.5 million trust fund left to him by his parents to hire legal representation as he faces murder charges in their deaths. The younger Reiner is seeking to use the inheritance to retain high-powered attorneys for his defense.

The case involves the killings of Nick Reiner's parents, who had established the trust for their son. Legal experts note the unusual nature of a defendant seeking to use funds from victims to mount a defense against charges related to those same victims' deaths. Rob Reiner is known for directing films including When Harry Met Sally and A Few Good Men.

cards.headline: Chanel Partners to Reopen Historic Paris Cinema
cards.teaser: The luxury fashion house is leading an effort to revive the Saint-Germain-des-Prés cinema, one of the most storied venues in Paris film history.
cards.body:
Chanel has joined a coalition of French business, publishing, and film figures to reopen the historic Saint-Germain-des-Prés cinema on Paris's Left Bank. The luxury house serves as the lead partner in the revival of the venue, which holds significant cultural importance in French cinema history.

The theater returned to public life last week with a gala event marking its reopening. The Saint-Germain-des-Prés cinema had been a landmark destination for cinephiles before its closure. The partnership bringing together multiple sectors of French culture and commerce reflects the venue's status in Parisian artistic life.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Reboot Tops U.K. Box Office
cards.teaser: The Paramount franchise revival opened in first place with $5.6 million across the U.K. and Ireland.
cards.body:
Paramount's Scary Movie reboot secured the top position at the U.K. and Ireland box office with a debut of $5.6 million. The franchise revival led a competitive weekend for theatrical releases in the region.

The Amazing Digital Circus: The Last Act from Piece Of Magic Entertainment opened in second place with $3.6 million. Fantasy film Masters Of The took the third position. The box office performance comes as theaters prepare for other major releases in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: Paramount Seeks Business Executive to Work with CBS News Chief Bari Weiss
cards.teaser: The media company is searching for a leader to help manage CBS News alongside its editor in chief.
cards.body:
Paramount Skydance has been recruiting a business executive to work with Bari Weiss, the editor in chief of CBS News. The position would involve managing operations at one of the nation's prominent news brands under Weiss's editorial leadership.

The role requires long hours and a flexible schedule while working with an editorial chief known for generating public discussion. The search reflects Paramount's efforts to structure the leadership team at CBS News following recent organizational changes. Weiss took the helm of CBS News as part of broader shifts in the network's management.

cards.headline: South Korean Director Lee Chang-dong to Receive Lifetime Achievement Award
cards.teaser: The filmmaker will be honored at Malaysia's MIFFest, which unveiled its program featuring 65 films from 35 countries.
cards.body:
Lee Chang-dong will receive the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 9th Malaysia International Film Festival. The recognition comes as the festival announced its full program in Kuala Lumpur, featuring 65 films from 35 countries and regions in 27 languages.

MIFFest runs from July 18 to 25 and will present two world premieres and one international premiere among its selections. Lee is known for acclaimed films that have earned recognition at major international festivals. The Malaysian festival's program spans diverse languages and cinematic traditions from across the globe.

cards.headline: Chaka Khan and Simple Minds to Headline Radio 2 in the Park
cards.teaser: The BBC festival will take place over three days in September in Stirling, Scotland.
cards.body:
Chaka Khan and Simple Minds will headline Radio 2 in the Park, the BBC's flagship music festival. The event runs from September 11-13 at City Park in Stirling.

The three-day festival brings together established artists across different genres for outdoor performances, continuing Radio 2 in the Park's tradition as a major fixture in the British summer festival calendar.

hero.headline: NRCC chairman defends Trump after midterm comments spark concern
hero.teaser: Rep. Richard Hudson said President Trump's recent comment about not caring about midterms has been misinterpreted.
hero.body:
National Republican Congressional Committee chairman Rep. Richard Hudson said Tuesday that President Trump's comment suggesting he does not care about midterms has been misinterpreted. Speaking at Axios AM Live, Hudson said Trump cares deeply about the upcoming elections.

The president's military actions in Iran have contributed to rising prices, raising concern among Republicans that unfulfilled promises to address cost-of-living issues could cost the party control of the Senate and House. Hudson told Axios that the world is safer because of Trump's actions.

cards.headline: House takes up reconciliation bill as Republicans weigh immigration enforcement votes
cards.teaser: The House of Representatives began consideration of a reconciliation bill on Tuesday, as Republican leaders work to secure support for a separate immigration en.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives began consideration of a reconciliation bill on Tuesday. Republican leaders are working to secure support for a separate immigration enforcement measure, though party leaders remain uncertain whether they have enough votes to pass it.

President Trump said late Monday that two crew members aboard a U.S. attack helicopter that crashed near the Strait of Hormuz are "fine." The AH-64 Apache helicopter was patrolling regional waters when it went down near the Oman coast, according to U.S. Central Command.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, secured the Democratic nomination for governor of New Mexico on Tuesday. She defeated other candidates in the primary election to become her party's nominee for the general election.

If elected in November, Haaland could make history as the first female Native American governor. The general election will determine whether she succeeds the current administration in leading the state.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California gubernatorial primary race
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading as votes are counted in California's primary for governor.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading California's gubernatorial primary election. Other candidates in the race include Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer, along with Republican Chad Bianco, all competing for their party's nominations to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.

California's top-two primary system advances the two candidates with the highest vote totals to the general election, regardless of party affiliation. Results continue to update as votes are counted across the state.

cards.headline: Trump calls NBA a little left wing after being booed at Finals game
cards.teaser: President Trump responded to being booed at Game 3 of the NBA Finals by calling the league a little left-wing but also great.
cards.body:
President Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to attend an NBA Finals game, appearing at Game 3 between the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Monday. When he was shown on the jumbotron during the national anthem, the crowd booed loudly for several seconds while Trump maintained a salute and smile. The boos quickly turned to cheers when Knicks players appeared on screen moments later.

After leaving the game, Trump responded to the hostile reception by telling reporters that the NBA was "a little left wing" while also describing it as "great." His attendance at the high-profile event drew increased security measures, with ticketholders required to pass through airport-style screening to enter the venue.

cards.headline: 35 former judges criticize Trump self-settlement as fraudulent
cards.teaser: A group of 35 former judges argued that a purported settlement of a case involving President Trump was the product of collusion and fraud.
cards.body:
Thirty-five former judges have publicly criticized what they describe as a fraudulent self-settlement involving President Trump. The former judges argued that the purported settlement of the case resulted from collusion and fraud.

The group of retired jurists issued their statement challenging the legitimacy of the settlement arrangement. They contend that the process violated legal standards and proper procedures for resolving the case.

cards.headline: Trump appointee Bill Pulte named director of national intelligence
cards.teaser: President Trump appointed Bill Pulte as interim director of national intelligence despite his lack of intelligence or national security experience.
cards.body:
President Trump named Bill Pulte as interim director of national intelligence, despite Pulte having no background in intelligence or national security. The appointment places Pulte in charge of overseeing the nation's intelligence agencies and coordinating their activities.

The stated reason for Pulte's appointment is to investigate claims that the 2020 presidential election was stolen. Pulte will serve in an interim capacity heading the intelligence community while pursuing this goal.
